talk.title: My grandfather's store
talk.task: Memory game: “I went to my grandfather's store and bought an apple, some bread, a camel…”
talk.claudePrompt: You are my partner in the memory game 'My Grandfather's Store'. We take turns. Each turn repeats the whole list and adds one new thing in alphabetical order (A, then B, then C...), using a, an or some: 'I went to my grandfather's store and bought an apple.' / '... an apple and some bread.' / '... an apple, some bread, and a camel.' You start with A. Check that I use a/an with singular count nouns and some with plural or noncount nouns.

talk.title: General statements
talk.task: Make general statements about wild animals (a/an), inventions (plural), and the rich or the elderly.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. I am practicing generic nouns. Ask me for: (1) three general statements about wild animals using a/an (A giraffe has a long neck.), (2) three general statements about inventions using the plural (Smartphones are useful.), (3) three general statements about the rich, the poor or the elderly. Check that I do not use 'the' with plural or noncount nouns when I generalize.

levels.title: Extra words don't decide

items.title: A long description can still be a
lines: More words don't make a noun special.

examples.text: Do you have a pen with red ink?

talk.title: Interview
talk.task: Claude asks: Do you have a pet? What is the name of your pet? Answer in full sentences.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. Ask me these pairs of questions one pair at a time: Do you have siblings? What are the names of your brothers and sisters? / Do you have a pet? What is the name of your pet? / What is your favorite restaurant? Where is the restaurant? / Think of a color. What is the color you first thought of? / Where is a fun place to go on weekends? / How is the weather in your hometown this time of year? I answer in complete sentences. Check my articles: a/an for first mention, the for second mention and things we both know.

talk.title: What happened to the…?
talk.task: Something got broken and it isn't yours! Tell Claude what happened.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. Role-play: you notice that something of mine is damaged (a phone screen, a bike, a laptop). Start with 'What happened to the ...? The ... is broken.' I explain what happened ('I dropped it. Even worse, it doesn't belong to me. It is my brother's.'). Ask 'What are you going to do?' Check my use of a/an for new things and the for things already mentioned.

talk.title: Travel brochure
talk.task: Pick a place people should visit. Tell Claude its points of interest and one thing not to miss.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English writing partner. Ask me to choose a city or region tourists would enjoy and write a mini travel brochure: three points of interest, two interesting facts, and a 4-5 sentence description of one place 'not to be missed'. Check my articles with geographic names (no 'the' with cities, countries, lakes and single mountains; 'the' with rivers, seas, oceans, mountain ranges and island groups).

talk.title: My “aha” moment

talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. Ask me one question at a time about my language learning: How much English do you speak and read outside class? Do you listen to the radio or podcasts in English? Is using English outside class important for you? What technique has helped you most? Have you had an 'aha' moment when something suddenly became clear? Check my article usage (a/an, the, or no article).
